name: What type of drywall is needed for bathrooms, basements, and garages?

mainEntity.name: What type of drywall is needed for bathrooms, basements, and garages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard dry areas use regular 1/2-inch gypsum drywall, but moist spaces like bathrooms, laundry rooms, and basements require moisture-resistant drywall, often called green board or purple board. Inside wet areas like walk-in showers or behind tub surrounds, drywall should never be used; instead, cement board or specialized waterproof tile backer boards must be installed. For garage fire separation walls or shared partitions, local residential building codes typically mandate 5/8-inch Type X fire-rated drywall to improve fire resistance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Bathrooms and basements need moisture-resistant drywall, showers require waterproof cement backer board, and garage shared walls typically require 5/8-inch Type X fire-rated drywall.
